rationale: Evidence: iteration 8 (kd 2.5, base_speed 1.2, kp 3.5, ki 0, 12 mm sensors at y=0.04 with x in ±0.04) is the best design tested, at 395.3. Its oval finishes 20 of 20 trials at mean time 1.87 s. Its s-bend (progress 0.395) and slalom (progress 0.178) still end off track with about one line-loss event per run. Iteration 9 (kd 3.2) and iteration 10 (kd 3.2, base_speed 1.4) returned metrics identical to iteration 8 on every track, so kd beyond 2.5 and the base_speed change show no measurable effect at this operating point. The kd trend (0.8 to 1.2 gives 57, 1.8 gives 340, 2.5 gives 395) has saturated. Earlier geometry changes (sensor span, sensor size, forward position, track and mass) all failed to move the s-bend beyond about 0.15 progress when damping was low, and they have not been tested with high damping. This is the final iteration and the final race runs on unseen tracks. The evidence does not support an untested change, and a change that breaks the oval finish would cost more than a speculative gain on the s-bend or slalom would add. I therefore deliver the best-tested design, iteration 8's geometry and controller, unchanged. Expected result: oval completion around 1.87 s, with the s-bend and slalom ending off track as before. Expected score is about 395 on the development tracks. Unseen-track performance is uncertain.
